title: 8th Sitting of third session of 2025
summary: Deputy Speaker Ahmed Nazim chaired a sitting that opened at 09:02 with 28 members present. After routine items (minutes of the first four sittings accepted, committee seat swaps announced), Thoddoo MP Hussain Sameer put two questions to the Culture Minister about items cleared out of Daarul Aasaar, and over twenty other members then asked about heritage sites in their areas, oral history, scholarships and the ministry's work. First readings of a Special Economic Zones Act amendment and a resolution on Aasandha cover for foreign spouses were announced, and debate began on a bill letting terminally ill pension members draw on their retirement savings; the debate was unfinished and no vote was taken in this part. This part opens at the end of the debate on a bill to amend the Pension Act, where members argued over whether the pension fund should be opened up for serious illness; debate was closed and the vote time is to be announced later. Parliament then debated a motion from North Galolhu MP Mohamed Ibrahim to gauge MPs' views on the difficulty of getting blood in the Maldives, especially for thalassemia patients. MDP and some other members backed it, while several PNC members said the government is already acting on it. The vote on the motion was not held because the required number of members was not present, and the sitting was adjourned to 21 October 2025 at 9:00. The text is partly garbled, so some positions are summarised loosely.

speakers.name: Adam Naseer Ibrahim
positions: Said items removed from Daarul Aasaar were classed as junk under the Public Finance Act and disposal rules, and no heritage item was discarded.
Described the ministry's work as oral history recording, a heritage framework, a bill on heritage symbols and signature research scholarships.
Said the barrier at Daarul Aasaar's entrance was not put up by his ministry and that no outer-wall work was under way.

speakers.name: Hussain Sameer
positions: Asked if records, photos or video were kept of the 12 lorry loads removed from Daarul Aasaar, and how items were judged junk.
Asked what was done for a Thoddoo heritage site, and why a black coral-stone area at Daarul Aasaar is left open to rain.
Said the old mosque in Ukulhas is decaying and asked why heritage sites in Thoddoo, Ukulhas and Rasdhoo, popular with tourists, are not prioritised.
Backed the motion; said the problem is long-running and described an island family struggling to find blood donors, pushing families to move to Male'.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Asked about restoring heritage buildings in his area, including a Kendhoo shrine and the historic Kudarikilu mosque.
Asked which island heritage repairs are complete, and how Thulhaadhoo lacquerwork quality will be maintained given worry about foreign workers doing it.
On the pension bill, supported the amendment, said pensions mainly secure old-age income, and urged the President to direct the PNC group to back it.
Said blood access is a real shortfall: donation rates are low, storage and logistics are weak, and he cited a post alleging blood being sold for thousands.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Asked what the ministry's 2025 budget will fund, whether more budget will be needed, and what work will be done within it.
Repeatedly asked who put up the barriers closing off the front of Daarul Aasaar for a long time, and when they will be removed.
Asked for details of work on Daarul Aasaar's outer wall and for what purpose barriers were put up outside it.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Asked whether the ministry has a website and what state it is in today.
Asked whether a searchable digital archive of Maldivian history documents exists or is planned, and how much of the President's address pledges is done.
On the pension bill, supported it: retirement savings are small and terminally ill members should be able to use their own money for care.
On the pension bill: asked for clarity on early access to the fund for terminal illness or disability, backed by a doctor's letter, as in other countries.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Asked why the minister, often seen in traditional dress before taking office, now wears a suit although a national dress exists.
As sponsor of the pension bill, said it would let members with terminal illness draw on retirement savings for care, with rules for claims.
On the pension bill: argued terminal-illness access needs proper systems, since Aasandha and ENSPA help is hard to get for ordinary people.
Introduced the blood motion, citing the lack of a national blood plan, weak donor registration and awareness, and thalassemia patients' struggle to get blood.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Asked how long it takes and how much it costs to 'build minds', which the minister named as a main policy.
Said part of his first question on that cost went unanswered, and asked how many political appointees serve the ministry and what they cost.
On the pension bill, began by supporting the intent of the amendment; his remarks continue beyond this part.
Backed the motion; said promises of a thalassemia hospital remain unmet and that medicine shortages and patients moving between pharmacies continue.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Asked what heritage work is under way in Maradhoo and whether historic sites are being damaged by the Gan airport development project in Addu City.
Asked whether the ATC tower in Addu, reportedly the first national building, is treated as heritage, given reports it may be demolished.
Asked whether any work is planned to protect Maldivian dialects, and about the barrier placed in front of the ministry.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Asked whether heritage items brought to Male' could be returned to the islands they came from as tourism develops.
Asked when a shrine area in Dh. Maaenboodhoo, declared a heritage zone but in ruins, will be protected and whether a plan exists.

Said blood needs public awareness and cannot be supplied by any government alone; pointed to the thalassemia law amendment and expanding dialysis, and urged members not to erode trust in the health system.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Asked the minister to clarify reports about former ministry staff being refused entry and whether that followed the rules.
On the pension bill, backed strengthening Aasandha and NSPA for long-term illness care and questioned whether the amendment was made in good faith.
Said he could not support the motion, arguing it was framed to suggest government failure, and pointed to the President's visit to the thalassemia centre and its new director general and premises.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Asked what the ministry has done to protect and maintain the Landhoo Mabadi heritage site.
On the pension bill, said drawing on the pension fund is not the best route and urged better health insurance and regional hospitals.
Backed the motion; said Velidhoo has thalassemia patients but no blood bank or donation programme, and asked for the regional hospital to be made ready.

speakers.name: Mohamed Dawoodh
positions: Said past governments did little to protect island heritage, especially in Kulhudhuffushi, and asked what plans past and current governments have.
Asked about a Daarul Aasaar-style museum in Kulhudhuffushi, listing its Tharijehige in a heritage register, and protecting intangible heritage items.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Noted a 2010 agreement with Israel on culture and one with East Timor, and asked about such agreements with states that have no Islamic background.
Said he does not support the pension amendment as proposed and asked its sponsor to reconsider and withdraw it, since pension funds are not used like this elsewhere.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Asked what advances have been made in the heritage sector over the past year.
Urged keeping the blood debate out of party politics, backed volunteer blood donation, and said the government is expanding dialysis and health services in the atolls.

speakers.name: Ahmed Naseer
positions: Asked what the newly announced signature research scholarships in the heritage sector are meant to achieve.
Said the motion was not needed as the government already runs blood drives and works on the issue; also said medicine supply problems predate this government.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Agreed long-term illness costs are a real problem but opposed paying for care from the pension fund, saying it exists to secure retirement income.
Suggested handling long-term care through Aasandha, NSPA and the universal health coverage system.
Said the blood problem needs a fix rather than a debate about which government did what, and urged building systems so people need not plead for help.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Said he could not support using pension money for treatment, arguing long-term care should be arranged through NSPA or Aasandha.
Said retirees' pensions are small and the retirement system itself needs reform.
Said the motion's real aim is blood access after accidents or major operations, not thalassemia alone, and suggested awareness drives and donor programmes by groups as well as the state.

speakers.name: Ahmed Xamyr
positions: Asked what the ministry has done to involve people in heritage and how many people have received awareness through its programmes.

speakers.name: Ahmed Zahir
positions: Asked whether the ministry plans heritage protection centres in the atolls.

speakers.name: Abdulla Shareef
positions: Asked how the Oral History project is going and how heritage work planned in Kelaa is scheduled.

speakers.name: Ahmed Riyaz
positions: Asked why a separate ministry was created for heritage, and what its main work and purpose are.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Asked what the ministry will do to stop the Dhivehi language fading and what counts as Dhivehi in its work.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Asked what the new ministry does now and what work is being done to develop the heritage sector.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Asked what heritage protection work is being done or planned in Fuvahmulah.

speakers.name: Asadhulla Shihab
positions: Asked whether the ministry has or is considering a procedure to relocate a shrine to Deevadhoo, as residents of that island have requested.

speakers.name: Ashraf Rasheed
positions: Asked when the old Boduatige in Faresmaathodaa, once a school, office and court and now in ruins, will be repaired.

speakers.name: Ahmed Azaan Marzooq
positions: On the pension bill: the pension fund is meant for retirement and should not be used for other costs; health cover like Aasandha or ENSPA should handle serious illness instead.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Defended the government's health record, citing bone marrow treatment support abroad and a new dedicated centre in Hulhumale'.
Said the previous administration left about MVR 1.5 billion in unpaid Aasandha bills, and urged MPs to donate blood.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ismail
positions: Called the issue sensitive but said he would not support the motion, arguing it appeared aimed at pressuring the government and that blood and medicine gaps predate it.

speakers.name: Ali Fazad
positions: Agreed with the Baarashu member; said the government knows the difficulties and passed an amendment to the Thalassemia Control Act on 6 August 2025.

decisions: Minutes of sittings 2025/3/1 to 2025/3/4 were declared accepted because no member proposed amendments.

Committee changes announced: Faresmaathodaa MP Ashraf Rasheed replaces North Hithadhoo MP Mohamed Sinan, and Guraidhoo MP Hanan Mohamed Rasheed replaces Mulaku MP Ibrahim Naufal, on the Independent Institutions Committee from 16 Oct 2025.
Committee deadline for the resolution on the Fenaka Corporation special audit report announced as 31 Oct 2025.
First reading announced of the government bill amending the Special Economic Zones Act (Law 24/2014).
First reading announced of a resolution seeking members' views on Aasandha cover for foreigners married to Maldivians.
Debate on the bill to amend the Pension Act was closed; the chair said the time of the vote would be announced later.
Debate on the blood-access motion was closed; no vote was held because the number of members required for a vote was not present (the chair cited 47 and 17 members on official travel).
Debate on the human organ transplant bill (item 9.1) was closed with no member asking to speak and its sponsor absent.
Item 10 (matters from committees) was not taken up for the same quorum reason.
The sitting was adjourned to Tuesday 21 October 2025 at 9:00; a lunch break ran 11:52 to 13:00.
